newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Sept Ifo climate index up.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Sept Ifo climate index up.

text.p: Following are comments from economists on the September Ifo West German business climate index, which rose to 95.7 from 94.4.
The Ifo index is regarded as a key reflection of business confidence. In August, the index rose to 94.4 from 94.0 in July.

"This was slightly above our forecast of 94.7. It fits in quite well with the forecast that after the rise in August there would be another rise. It must be seen that this is still some 10 percent below the highest level at the end of 1994.
"There is a long way to go before overheating."
"We did have a forecast of 95.5 so this fits in with the gradual improvement, the recovery that is still going on. What this does show is that the eastern part is lagging."
(East German index was at 104, up from 103.9).

"This is totally consistent with the view of the economy in the Bundesbank's recent monthly report. It will not change the steady policy which it is following. There is no reason to think about a repo rate cut. A tightening will not be for some months either."
"It is not a disappointment. We had expected 95 to 96. We can see now that the order intake from foreign countries had had a positive impact on expectations."
Uwe Angenendt, BHF Bank in Frankfurt

"It was slightly higher than expected, we had expected a figure of up to 95.5. It reflects the trend shown in order and production data which showed a fairly strong rise in July and August. We think the increases will continue and expect quarter-on-quarter GDP growth of about one percent in the third quarter after 1.5 percent in the second quarter. That's a fairly favourable environment for the economy. We already believed before this number that the Bundesbank had no reason to lower interest rates.
